title: Pollen became easier to account for
summary:
This week made the unified API easier to understand and harder to trip over, from Pollen accounting and model routing to image, video, and concurrent requests.

Usage gained a JSON and CSV API, timestamp pagination, and a dashboard download. Enter now shows recent spend pending against balances and includes it in balance checks. New accounts are assigned the SPORE tier automatically, removing a manual activation step. The result is a clearer answer to two practical questions: what did my requests cost, and what can I use next?

`gemini` and `gemini-search` now route to Gemini 3 Flash Preview, while `gemini-fast` routes to Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite. `gemini-large` supplies Search and URL Context by default unless callers provide their own tools. Reasoning-model temperature handling now accounts for resolved aliases, avoiding unsupported-value errors; chat also gained `repetition_penalty`, and `openai-audio` accepts its listed voices.

Z-Image now respects requested proportions and improves backgrounds and detected faces. Seedance Pro passes through aspect ratios, Seedream 4.5 Pro passes through seeds, and Veo can use a supplied image as its first frame. Gemini chat requests can include a video URL alongside text. Reference-image URLs with their own query parameters work too, while Veo prompt and policy failures return a more useful HTTP 400.

API keys can be limited to selected text, image, and video models, with permissions checked after aliases resolve. The dashboard restored full publishable-key copying and made key previews clearer. Text and image playgrounds now distinguish denied requests from rate limits and other errors; image generation can retry when a retry delay is supplied. Hello also runs theme design, copy, and background requests in parallel.
